name: MathVista
description: MathVista is a benchmark designed to combine challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks. It consists of 6,141 examples, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets involving mathematics and 3 newly created datasets (i.e., IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). Completing these tasks requires fine-grained, deep visual understanding and compositional reasoning.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao (UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research)
citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2024.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering (MathQA) datasets and 19 VQA datasets. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure a balanced representation. In addition, three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA) were created to address missing types of mathematical reasoning over specific visual contexts. IQTest comprises 228 examples sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms. FunctionQA contains 400 examples sourced from functional plots. PaperQA includes 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface. For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were used to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning from a large pool of candidates (examples with numeric answers or containing quantity words). This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data was collected from 28 existing multimodal datasets (9 MathQA datasets and 19 VQA datasets). Three new datasets were created: IQTest (sourced from puzzle test figures on online learning platforms), FunctionQA (functional plots), and PaperQA (academic papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface).
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers released in August 2023 for PaperQA. Timeframe for other source datasets not specified.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules were designed to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning (examples with numeric answers or those containing quantity words). This automatic filtration yielded 4,949 VQA-format examples. Three expert annotators manually labeled these examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. Utilizing majority voting and limiting each source dataset to 400 examples, a final collection of 2,739 examples was obtained. Each source dataset is limited to up to 400 examples to ensure balanced representation. Questions with a length greater than 60 are categorized as 61 for visualization simplicity.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three expert annotators manually labeled VQA examples to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. Annotators were trained using detailed instructions and examples. Three labeling options were provided: Yes (involves mathematical reasoning), No (does not involve mathematical reasoning), and Unsure (use sparingly). Majority voting was used to finalize labels. For the three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, PaperQA), all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process. A two-step process ensured consistency: initially, each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers, resulting in a 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate. Discrepancies (6 out of 736 questions) were resolved through discussion among the entire review team. Metadata annotations (question type, answer type, task, grade level, visual context, mathematical reasoning) were automatically obtained from source dataset details. To verify automatic annotation quality, expert annotators manually labeled mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples, showing 94.1% exact match and 98.79% individual label agreement.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool (GUI shown in Figure 23 and Figure 24)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A preliminary study of 200 examples shows that GPT-4 can extract the answer text with more than 99.5% accuracy. Inter-annotator agreement analysis among three annotators yielded a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial consistency. Among 736 newly collected questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in annotated answers. For automatic metadata annotation verification, 94.1% of examples from automatic and human annotations have the exact same set of reasoning types, while 98.79% of individual labels are identical.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields for new datasets. Expert annotators with satisfactory annotating history for VQA labeling. Human performance baseline annotators from Amazon Mechanical Turk with high school diploma or higher, satisfactory annotating history, and successful completion of qualification examples.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 for answer extraction from model responses. EasyOCR for OCR text detection. Multimodal Bard for image caption generation.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that questions are biased toward North American educational standards and may not represent global curricula. English-only sources limit cross-lingual generalization. The dataset features 6.57% non-English questions (including Chinese and Persian), but the majority is English. GPT-4V's self-verification is weaker for non-English tasks such as Mandarin.
rai:dataLimitations: While MathVista encompasses a broad spectrum of tasks and visual contexts, there may be gaps in the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. The dataset's focus on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, necessitates a more labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data compared to textual-only or general-purpose datasets. Scalability and generalizability to other domains remain a concern. Annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations. Due to heterogeneity of sources, annotations lack a unified format and structure. The study focused exclusively on the most recent and prominent models. Most academic papers do NOT discuss maintenance plans, versioning schedules, or deprecation policies. A statement like 'the dataset is publicly available' is NOT a maintenance plan.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating mathematical reasoning of foundation models in visual contexts. Use cases include: Training, Testing, Validation of large language models (LLMs) and large multimodal models (LMMs) for tasks such as figure question answering (FQA), geometry problem solving (GPS), math word problem (MWP), textbook question answering (TQA), and visual question answering (VQA). The benchmark is intended to facilitate the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks.
